====================================================================
Empirical Research Plan:  “Can Media Coverage Alone Move Stock Prices?
Evidence from the 1998 EntreMed / New-York-Times Episode”
====================================================================


--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Method:  Difference-in-Differences (DiD) combined with a short-horizon
event study.

Rationale  
1. The May-4 price reaction is a textbook “event.”  A 3-day window
   (May 1–5) isolates the shock while limiting exposure to other news.
2. To attribute the reaction to the *media* (and not to coincident
   market movements or a latent biotech re-valuation) we compare ENMD
   to (i) the biotech index, (ii) size-, beta-, and R&D-matched biotech
   firms, and (iii) the broad market.  
3. DiD exploits cross-section (treated vs. controls) and time (pre vs.
   post article) variation.  Under parallel-trend assumptions, the DiD
   coefficient identifies the causal effect of the NYT article on
   ENMD’s abnormal return and abnormal volume.  
4. A companion event-study (market-model abnormal returns) provides the
   traditional finance benchmark and a placebo (Nature-publication) test
   strengthens causal claims.

Why appropriate  
• The media article is plausibly exogenous to ENMD’s fundamentals
  because the underlying science was already public for five months.  
• Daily CRSP and Lexis-Nexis data give us sufficiently high-frequency
  observations to cleanly bracket the shock.  
• Multiple untreated yet similar firms allow construction of a credible
  counterfactual price path.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
TREAT_i,t = 1 for ENMD on or after Monday, 4-May-1998; 0 otherwise.

Control groups  
1. Biotech index (NASDAQ Biotechnology Index or equal-weighted set).  
2. Matched controls: each ENMD observation is matched to the average of
   3–5 Nasdaq-listed biotech firms with closest market-cap, cash-to-
   assets, and R&D-to-assets as of April-1998, but **without any NYT
   coverage on May-3**.  
3. Broad-market benchmark: S&P 500 constituents.

Timing / Variation  
•  Event window: [−10, +10] trading days around May-4.  
•  Estimation (pre) window for market-model betas: [−120, −30] days.  
•  Placebo event: identical windows around 27-Nov-1997 (Nature).
  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends (common shocks)   
   In the absence of the NYT article, ENMD’s return would have moved in
   line with controls over the short horizon.  
   Plausibility: High for a 20-day window; biotech controls share
   systematic risk factors.

A2. No simultaneous confounders  
   No ENMD-specific fundamental information arrived exactly on May-4.  
   Plausibility: Very high—the scientific finding was old; SEC filings
   and PR wires show no other releases.

A3. No anticipation / information leakage  
   Market did not learn about the NYT article before the close on
   Friday, May-1.  
   Plausibility: Supported by negligible abnormal volume/return on
   May-1; Sunday print timing limits leakage.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA)  
   Effects on ENMD do not spill heavily to controls (or spillovers are
   limited and measurable).  
   Plausibility: Some small spillover to biotech index likely; we test
   robustness using only non-oncology biotech controls.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Other contemporaneous biotech news (e.g., FDA actions)  
   • Mitigation: Search Lexis-Nexis, PRNewswire, and FDA archives for
     May 1-5; exclude any firm/event with overlapping news.  Include day
     fixed effects to soak up market-wide shocks.

T2. Market over-reaction and reversal (behavioral bias vs. media)  
   • Mitigation: Track cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) through +30
     days.  If price fully reverses after attention wanes, this supports
     attention-induced mispricing rather than fundamentals.

T3. Spillovers to control firms violate SUTVA  
   • Mitigation: Use two separate control sets (industry vs. outside
     industry).  If DiD estimates are similar, spillovers are unlikely
     to drive results.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(lmtest); library(sandwich)  # robust SEs
library(fixest)                    # fast DiD regression

# ---- 1. Data Loading ----
## Assume: crsp_daily.csv (permno, date, ret, vol, prc, shrout)
##         firm_info.csv   (permno, cusip, sic, mktcap, rd_assets)
##         nytimes_event.csv (date_event)  # holds the two event dates
crsp <- read_csv("crsp_daily.csv") %>%
          mutate(date = ymd(date))

info <- read_csv("firm_info.csv")

events <- tibble(event = c("nature", "nyt"),
                 date_event = as_date(c("1997-11-27", "1998-05-04")))

# ---- 2. Treatment Definition ----
## Identify ENMD permno
enmd_permno <- info %>% filter(cusip == "29382F10") %>% pull(permno)

crsp <- crsp %>%
  mutate(treat_firm = if_else(permno == enmd_permno, 1, 0),
         biotech = if_else(str_sub(sic,1,2) %in% c("28"), 1, 0))

# ---- 3. Build Matched Controls ----
## Simple nearest-neighbor on April-1998 market cap & R&D
match_candidates <- info %>%
  filter(biotech == 1, permno != enmd_permno) %>%
  mutate(rank = abs(log(mktcap) - log(filter(info, permno==enmd_permno)$mktcap))) %>%
  arrange(rank) %>% slice(1:5) %>% pull(permno)

crsp <- crsp %>%
  mutate(control = if_else(permno %in% match_candidates, 1, 0))

# ---- 4. Construct Event Window Variables ----
main_event <- events %>% filter(event=="nyt") %>% pull(date_event)
crsp <- crsp %>%
  mutate(post = if_else(date >= main_event & date <= main_event + days(2), 1, 0),
         window_20 = if_else(date >= main_event - days(10) &
                             date <= main_event + days(10), 1, 0))

# Restrict to event window
evdata <- crsp %>% filter(window_20 == 1,
                          treat_firm==1 | control==1) %>%
          left_join(info %>% select(permno, sic))

# ---- 5. Regression: Difference-in-Differences on Returns ----
did_model <- feols(ret ~ treat_firm*post | date + permno,
                   data = evdata,
                   cluster = ~permno)

summary(did_model)

# ---- 6. Robustness: Placebo Nature Event ----
placebo_event <- events %>% filter(event=="nature") %>% pull(date_event)

evdata_placebo <- crsp %>%
  mutate(post_placebo = if_else(date >= placebo_event &
                                date <= placebo_event + days(2), 1, 0),
         window_20_p = if_else(date >= placebo_event - days(10) &
                               date <= placebo_event + days(10), 1, 0)) %>%
  filter(window_20_p==1, treat_firm==1 | control==1)

placebo <- feols(ret ~ treat_firm*post_placebo | date + permno,
                 data = evdata_placebo,
                 cluster = ~permno)
summary(placebo)
```
(The same procedure can be repeated for abnormal trading volume.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
• Main effect (ENMD × Post) on daily return should be strongly positive  
  – Rough prior: +300% raw ≈ +2.0 to +2.5 when expressed in log-return
  terms on May-4, with cumulative abnormal return of ~250–300% over the
  three-day window.  
• Controls should show at most a modest bump (5–15%).  
• Placebo (Nature) DiD coefficient near zero.  
• Volume results: ENMD’s share turnover multiples of 50× normal.

Economic interpretation: Media attention, even without incremental
information, can temporarily decouple prices from fundamentals.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = satisfied, 0 = weak)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Parallel-trend evidence in pre-period          … 1  
2. No simultaneous confounders                    … 0.8  
3. No anticipation / leakage                      … 0.9  
4. Limited spillovers / SUTVA                     … 0.7  
5. Robustness to alternative controls & windows   … 1  
TOTAL (average)                                   … 0.88

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
--------------------------------------------------------------------
